Governance Risk Compliance

Access Certification

A formal, periodic review process in which managers or data owners attest that users have the appropriate levels of access to systems and information according to their roles and responsibilities.

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Access Certification?

In this glossary, Access Certification refers to: A formal, periodic review process in which managers or data owners attest that users have the appropriate levels of access to systems and information according to their roles and responsibilities.

How is Access Certification used in cybersecurity?

In cybersecurity communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "Regular access certification helps organizations reduce the risk of privilege creep and ensures only authorized personnel retain system access."

Why does Access Certification matter in cybersecurity?

Access Certification matters because it supports clear communication in Governance Risk Compliance contexts for SOC Analysts, Security Engineers, and Incident Responders. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as CISSP, CompTIA Security+, and CEH.

Who uses Access Certification?

Access Certification is mainly used by SOC Analysts, Security Engineers, and Incident Responders.

What category does Access Certification belong to?

In this glossary, Access Certification is grouped under Governance Risk Compliance. Related pages in this category explain adjacent procedures, commands and operational concepts.
